recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — name each move in order, and say which general solution formula you would use.

steps.label: Pair two terms
steps.margin_note: First mark. Bring everything to one side, then pair the two terms whose half-sum matches the third angle — here 2θ and 8θ average to 5θ, which is exactly the term left over.

recall.must_convey: That cos2θ and cos8θ are paired with the cos C + cos D formula, whose half-sum is 5θ.
accept: pair cos two theta and cos eight theta, their half sum is five theta which matches the other term
apply the cos C plus cos D formula to the first two
bring everything to one side and pair the two that average to five theta
modati rendu ni pair cheste half sum five theta vasthundi
use sum to product on the pair

steps.why: Pairing the RIGHT two terms is the whole skill: 2θ and 8θ average to 5θ, so a cos5θ appears and the equation gains a common factor. Any other pairing gives nothing.
common_mistakes: Leaving the cos5θ on the right-hand side.

steps.label: Factorise
steps.margin_note: Second mark. cos(−3θ) is cos3θ because cosine is even. Then cos5θ is common to both terms and comes out.

recall.must_convey: That cos(−3θ) = cos3θ and cos5θ is taken out as a common factor, splitting into two branches.
accept: cos of minus three theta is cos three theta then take cos five theta common giving two branches
factorise out cos five theta so either factor can be zero
cosine is even so the minus goes, then factor
cos minus three theta ante cos three theta, cos five theta common teeyyali
take the common factor and split into two cases

steps.why: A product is zero when either factor is zero, which is why factorising splits one equation into two independent ones. Each must then be solved separately.
common_mistakes: Cancelling cos5θ instead of factorising, which loses a whole family of solutions.

steps.label: Solve cos5θ = 0
steps.margin_note: Third mark. cosθ = 0 has its own general solution — (2n+1)π/2 — different from cosθ = cosα. Note the equation is in 5θ, so divide at the end.

accept: cos five theta equals zero gives five theta equals two n plus one pi by two so theta is two n plus one pi by ten
the cosine is zero so use the odd multiples of pi by two then divide by five
theta is two n plus one pi over ten
cos zero ki two n plus one pi by two, five tho divide cheste pi by ten
solve the first branch

steps.why: cos = 0 at every odd multiple of π/2, which is a different formula from cos = cos α. Using the wrong one here loses half the solutions.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to divide the whole right side by 5.

steps.label: Solve 2cos3θ = 1
steps.margin_note: Last mark. cos3θ = 1/2 = cos(π/3), so the cosine general solution applies — then divide through by 3.
lines: Here α = π/3, and for cosθ = cosα, θ = 2nπ ± α

recall.must_convey: That cos3θ = 1/2 gives 3θ = 2nπ ± π/3, so θ = 2nπ/3 ± π/9.
accept: cos three theta is a half which is cos pi by three so three theta is two n pi plus or minus pi by three and theta is two n pi by three plus or minus pi by nine
use the cosine general solution then divide by three
theta is two n pi over three plus or minus pi over nine
cos three theta half, general solution rasi three tho divide cheyyali
solve the second branch

steps.why: Both terms on the right must be divided by 3, not just one. Dividing only the α is the commonest slip in this whole chapter.
common_mistakes: Dividing only the π/3 and leaving 2nπ.
